questions.q: Why is the Earth called the 'Blue Planet'?
answer: The Earth is called the Blue Planet because most of its surface is covered by water, which gives it a blue appearance from space.

answer.text: About 71 per cent of the Earth's surface is water and only about 29 per cent is land. This dominance of water is unique among the planets we know.
Most of this water is salty ocean water; only a small fraction is fresh water, held in rivers, lakes, glaciers and underground. It is this fresh water that supports life on land.

answer: The vast oceans divide the land into continents and make Earth's surface look mainly blue.

questions.q: Describe the five oceans of the world in order of size.
answer: The world's single body of ocean water is divided into five oceans.

answer.text: The largest and deepest ocean, holding the Mariana Trench, the deepest known point on Earth.
The second largest, roughly 'S'-shaped, and the busiest for world trade.
The third largest and the only ocean named after a country, India.
The Southern (Antarctic) Ocean surrounds Antarctica, while the Arctic Ocean, around the North Pole, is the smallest and shallowest and is largely covered with ice.

questions.q: Describe the seven continents, noting a distinctive feature of each.

answer.text: The largest continent, home to India and to Mount Everest, the world's highest point.
The second largest; the Equator and both Tropics pass through it. It has the Sahara, the largest hot desert, and the Nile, the longest river.
Two continents of the western hemisphere; South America holds the Amazon river and rainforest.
Around the South Pole — the coldest continent, ice-covered, with no permanent human population.
Europe is joined to Asia to form Eurasia; Australia is the smallest continent and the only one that is also a single country.
